A small core for agent trust

Verify the message.
Choose who to trust.

Agents hear from people, services, and other agents. Developers need an easy way to check where those messages came from, without sharing secret keys with every source.

That’s why we built Marque. Sign with a private key. Verify the signing address. Apply your own rules for trust.

01 / How it works

One key signs.
Anyone can verify.

The sender keeps a private key. The receiver needs the message and signature, plus its own trust rules. A public address identifies the signing key.

01

Sign at the source

Marque signs your JSON payload with a recipient ID, expiry, and random nonce.

sign(payload, options)
02

Send it your way

Deliver the complete envelope through your existing API, inbox, or message queue.

JSON.stringify(message)
03

Verify before acting

Check the signature, recipient, time window, and nonce. Get the verified signing address.

verify(message, context)
↳

A valid signature proves control of a key. Your application decides who owns that address and what it may do. A signature alone does not establish identity, human approval, or safe content.

Inside the signed envelope 8 fields · v2 +

The signature covers marque/v2\n followed by canonical JSON of every field except sig: sorted object keys, compact values, and unchanged array order. Extra envelope fields are rejected.

Marque v2 envelope fields
FieldPurpose
vProtocol version. Currently 2.
signerThe sender’s public, 20-byte address.
audA case-sensitive recipient ID agreed by both applications.
ts / expIssued-at and expiry times in Unix seconds. Lifetime: 1–300 seconds; default 300.
nonce12 random bytes, used to reject the same message a second time.
payloadYour plain JSON message, signed directly.
sigA 65-byte recoverable signature, encoded as hex.

Marque uses secp256k1 and EIP-191 message signing. Verification recovers the public key, derives its address with Keccak-256, and checks it against signer. There is no blockchain transaction or domain lookup.

Use plain JSON payloads: no undefined, custom objects, sparse arrays, cycles, non-finite numbers, or unsafe integers. This canonical format is specific to Marque, not a full RFC 8785 implementation.

Expired messages and timestamps more than 300 seconds from the receiver’s clock are rejected. Keep clocks synchronized. V1 envelopes are not supported.

One-minute quickstart

Your first verified message.

In the Marque checkout, run the commands below. You’ll see a verified address, then tampering and replay rejected. The file includes every import and setup step.

npm ci npm run example
The complete example JavaScript +

Ephemeral key · local replay cache

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { createECDH } from 'node:crypto';
import { sign, verify } from '@jackmorganxyz/marque';

// Ephemeral demo key. Production keys belong in your application's secret store.
const key = createECDH('secp256k1');
key.generateKeys();
const privateKey = `0x${key.getPrivateKey('hex').padStart(64, '0')}`;
const message = await sign({ task: 'summarize', text: 'Hello' }, {
  privateKey, aud: 'bob-inbox',
});

// This demo trusts the key it just created. Never enroll keys from incoming messages.
const trustedAddresses = new Set([message.signer.toLowerCase()]);
// shortcut: process-local replay storage, replace with an atomic durable store before deployment.
const seen = new Map();
const consumeNonce = (key, expiresAt) => {
  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  for (const [k, expiry] of seen) if (expiry <= now) seen.delete(k);
  if (seen.has(key)) return false;
  seen.set(key, expiresAt);
  return true;
};

const received = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(message));
const context = { aud: 'bob-inbox', consumeNonce };
const result = await verify(received, context);
assert.equal(result.ok, true);
assert.equal(trustedAddresses.has(result.signer.toLowerCase()), true);
console.log('✓ Message verified from', result.signer);
assert.equal((await verify({ ...received, payload: 'tampered' }, context)).ok, false);
console.log('✓ Tampered message rejected');
assert.equal((await verify(received, context)).reason, 'replay');
console.log('✓ Replayed message rejected');

Receiver · verify, check trust, then apply permissions

import { verify } from '@jackmorganxyz/marque';

const result = await verify(message, {
  aud: 'bob-inbox',
  consumeNonce,
});

if (!result.ok) throw new Error('Invalid message');
if (!trustedAddresses.has(result.signer.toLowerCase())) {
  throw new Error('Untrusted sender');
}

// Validate the payload schema and this sender’s permissions.
// Only then let your agent act.
verify(message, { aud, consumeNonce, now? })Returns { ok: true, signer } or { ok: false, reason }.

Your app supplies the parsed message, trustedAddresses, and consumeNonce. Use your configured recipient ID for aud, never a value copied from the incoming message. Leave now unset to use the current clock; tests can override it with Unix seconds.

Understand a rejected message Typed reasons +

VerifyResult narrows on ok. Its reason uses the VerifyFailure union. Every failure rejects the message; use the reason to decide what to fix.

Failure reasons and next steps
ReasonNext step
wrong audienceMatch both applications’ configured recipient IDs.
expired / clock skewCheck clocks and delivery time. Check the operation’s status before retrying.
replayThe nonce was consumed. Use the operation ID to look up the result.
nonce store failedRestore storage and check the callback returns a boolean. Keep rejecting messages.
bad version / malformed envelopeDeliver the complete v2 envelope returned by sign.
signer mismatch / verification failedCheck for changed content, malformed signatures or unsupported JSON.
invalid verification contextSupply a nonempty audience, a nonce callback and a valid clock.

Read the agent instructions v2.0.0 +
# Build with Marque — core v2.0.0

Use `@jackmorganxyz/marque`. Core v2 is prepared but not yet on npm: install this local checkout with `npm install /absolute/path/to/marque`. Node.js 18+, ESM. The only runtime exports are `sign` and `verify`.

## API

- `await sign(payload, { privateKey, aud, ttl? })` returns a v2 `Signed` envelope. Supply plain JSON, a dedicated `0x`-prefixed 32-byte secp256k1 key, and a nonempty recipient ID. Lifetime is 1–300 seconds, default 300. Invalid input throws.
- `await verify(message, { aud, consumeNonce, now? })` returns `{ ok: true, signer }` or `{ ok: false, reason }`. Use the receiver’s configured audience, never an incoming value. Leave `now` unset outside tests; it is Unix seconds.
- `consumeNonce(key, expiresAt)` must atomically retain a new key until its Unix-seconds expiry, shared across all receivers and restarts. Return exactly `true` once, `false` for repeats; throw on storage errors. Verification returns `nonce store failed` on errors or non-boolean results.
- Types: `Hex`, `Address`, `Signed`, `VerifyFailure`, `VerifyResult`. Failure reasons: `invalid verification context`, `malformed envelope`, `bad version`, `wrong audience`, `expired`, `clock skew`, `signer mismatch`, `replay`, `nonce store failed`, `verification failed`.

## Application responsibilities

Keep keys outside prompts, logs and public bundles. Enroll public addresses through a trusted channel; compare lowercase addresses. A signature proves control of a key, not identity, permission or safe content. Never enroll an incoming sender automatically.

Limit request size and JSON depth before verification. After verification, check the address allowlist, action permissions and payload schema. Deliver the complete envelope over secure transport. No domain setup, identity service or blockchain is required.

Verification consumes a nonce before your handler runs. Use a signed operation ID and durable application idempotency for retries. A fresh signature is not proof that an operation is new. Reject on storage failure; never fall back to accepting messages or an in-memory cache.

The runnable Redis recipe is `examples/redis-receiver.mjs`; setup is in `docs/integration.md`. Keep Redis records until expiry, including through restarts, eviction pressure and failover. Use `examples/keygen.mjs` for local key setup. These are examples, not additional core APIs.

## Check your integration

Run `npm ci` and `npm run check` in the Marque checkout. With Redis running, set `REDIS_URL` and run `npm run test:redis`. Test valid messages, tampering, unknown senders, wrong audience, expiry, unavailable storage, concurrent replay and receiver restarts. Exactly one verification of an envelope may succeed. Never claim production readiness based only on the browser demo.

## Complete local example

Run `npm run example` in this checkout. The complete source is [examples/round-trip.mjs](../examples/round-trip.mjs); with Marque installed, save it as `quickstart.mjs` and run `node quickstart.mjs`. Its key and replay cache are deliberately temporary. The website's copy button includes the full file.

key.generateKeys();
const privateKey = `0x${key.getPrivateKey('hex').padStart(64, '0')}`;
const message = await sign({ task: 'summarize', text: 'Hello' }, {
  privateKey, aud: 'bob-inbox',
});

// This demo trusts the key it just created. Never enroll keys from incoming messages.
const trustedAddresses = new Set([message.signer.toLowerCase()]);
// shortcut: process-local replay storage, replace with an atomic durable store before deployment.
const seen = new Map();
const consumeNonce = (key, expiresAt) => {
  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  for (const [k, expiry] of seen) if (expiry <= now) seen.delete(k);
  if (seen.has(key)) return false;
  seen.set(key, expiresAt);
  return true;
};

const received = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(message));
const context = { aud: 'bob-inbox', consumeNonce };
const result = await verify(received, context);
assert.equal(result.ok, true);
assert.equal(trustedAddresses.has(result.signer.toLowerCase()), true);
console.log('✓ Message verified from', result.signer);
assert.equal((await verify({ ...received, payload: 'tampered' }, context)).ok, false);

assert.equal((await verify(received, context)).reason, 'replay');

04 / Your application

You build the trust layer.

Marque handles the cryptographic proof. These are the pieces to connect around it.

  1. 01

    Keys & enrollment

    Generate a dedicated secp256k1 key and supply it as 0x-prefixed, 32-byte hex. Keep it outside prompts, logs, and browser bundles. Exchange the public address through a trusted channel. Your app handles rotation and revocation.

  2. 02

    Trust & permissions

    Store approved addresses in lowercase. Decide which actions each address may request. Map addresses to people or accounts yourself. Never enroll a sender just because its signature verifies.

  3. 03

    Delivery & recipients

    Send the whole envelope over a secure transport. Agree on a specific aud for the destination. Forwarding does not change that recipient; a different recipient needs a new signed envelope.

  4. 04

    Replay storage

    Implement consumeNonce(key, expiresAt) with a shared, durable store. Atomically record an unused key until its Unix-seconds expiry. Return true only for the first use, false for repeats; throw on storage failure.

    Redis operation +
    SET marque:<key> 1 NX EXAT <expiresAt>

    Map Redis OK to true, and a missing result to false. All receiver instances must use the same store. Storage errors fail verification.

  5. 05

    Safe actions & retries

    Limit request size and depth. Validate the payload schema and permissions before acting. Signatures do not encrypt data or make instructions safe. Verification consumes the nonce; use an application operation ID to prevent duplicate actions on retries.

A runnable Redis receiver Copy the recipe +

This recipe reads a JSON envelope from stdin, verifies it against a configured audience, checks an address allowlist and validates one allowed action. Each process shares an atomic Redis nonce store. It prints accepted work for your application to dispatch.

From this checkout, with Redis running:

Local setup · refuses to overwrite .env.local

npm ci
node examples/keygen.mjs
set -a
. ./.env.local
set +a
export MARQUE_AUDIENCE=bob-inbox
export REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379
node examples/send.mjs | node examples/redis-receiver.mjs

examples/redis-receiver.mjs · node-redis 5

import { createClient } from 'redis';
import { verify } from '@jackmorganxyz/marque';

const { REDIS_URL, MARQUE_AUDIENCE, TRUSTED_ADDRESSES } = process.env;
const addresses = TRUSTED_ADDRESSES?.split(',').map(address => address.trim().toLowerCase());
if (!REDIS_URL || !MARQUE_AUDIENCE || !addresses?.length ||
    addresses.some(address => !/^0x[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(address))) {
  throw new Error('Set REDIS_URL, MARQUE_AUDIENCE and comma-separated TRUSTED_ADDRESSES');
}
const trustedAddresses = new Set(addresses);
let redis;

async function readMessage() {
  const chunks = [];
  let size = 0;
  for await (const chunk of process.stdin) {
    size += chunk.length;
    if (size > 16384) throw new Error('message too large');
    chunks.push(chunk);
  }
  const message = JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8'));
  function checkDepth(value, remaining) {
    if (remaining < 0) throw new Error('message too deep');
    if (value && typeof value === 'object')
      for (const child of Object.values(value)) checkDepth(child, remaining - 1);
  }
  checkDepth(message, 32);
  return message;
}

try {
  const message = await readMessage();
  try {
    redis = createClient({
      url: REDIS_URL, disableOfflineQueue: true,
      socket: { connectTimeout: 3000, reconnectStrategy: false },
    });
    // Required by node-redis; promise failures below reject without logging connection secrets.
    redis.on('error', () => {});
    await redis.connect();
  } catch { throw new Error('nonce store failed'); }
  const result = await verify(message, {
    aud: MARQUE_AUDIENCE,
    consumeNonce: async (key, expiresAt) => {
      const reply = await redis.withCommandOptions({ abortSignal: AbortSignal.timeout(3000) }).set(
        `marque:nonce:${key}`, '1', { condition: 'NX', expiration: { type: 'EXAT', value: expiresAt } },
      );
      if (reply !== 'OK' && reply !== null) throw new Error('unexpected nonce store response');
      return reply === 'OK';
    },
  });
  if (!result.ok) throw new Error(result.reason);
  if (!trustedAddresses.has(result.signer.toLowerCase())) throw new Error('untrusted sender');
  const payload = message.payload;
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object' || Array.isArray(payload) ||
      Object.keys(payload).length !== 3 ||
      typeof payload.id !== 'string' || !/^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i.test(payload.id) ||
      payload.task !== 'summarize' || typeof payload.text !== 'string' ||
      payload.text.length < 1 || payload.text.length > 2000) throw new Error('invalid payload');
  // Dispatch here only after persisting operation status by signer + payload.id for idempotent retries.
  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ signer: result.signer, payload }) + '\n');
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Rejected:', error instanceof SyntaxError ? 'invalid JSON' : error.message);
  process.exitCode = 1;
} finally {
  if (redis?.isOpen) redis.destroy();
}

In your own project, install Marque and redis@5. Keep the sender’s private key in its secret store; the receiver needs only approved public addresses. Use durable Redis with no nonce eviction or loss during failover. Apply transport timeouts and rate limits; persist operation IDs before dispatching work.

Before you ship

Test tampering, wrong recipients, expiry, and unknown senders. Replay the same envelope across instances and after a restart. Exactly one verification should succeed.

Small by design

Bring your agent.
Keep your architecture.

Use Marque for an agent inbox, a signed service message, or a login challenge. Identity, transport, and authorization stay in your application.
